learning: In Zig monorepos, cross-tree relative @import from script entrypoints can fail with 'import of file outside module path'; use named module imports wired in build.zig and keep workflows building via those steps.
evidence: Observed failure compiling apps/lift script after importing ../../../libs/core/src/io_helpers.zig directly; fixed by @import("core_io") + build.zig imports.
application: Define shared libs under libs/core and inject per-executable imports (core_io/core_json/core_path) in build graph; avoid direct zig build-exe against files requiring shared modules.

learning: Codified module-boundary guidance for shared Zig imports in monorepo migration docs.
evidence: Durable anchor: docs/migration/monorepo-plan.md (Import boundary rule).
application: Keep future CLI additions on named module imports wired in build.zig to avoid outside-module-path regressions.

learning: For independent CLI release automation in a Zig monorepo, keep a per-app VERSION file and enforce exact tag equality in each workflow before packaging assets.
evidence: zig build build-seq/build-lift/build-cas passed after adding VERSION checks and normalized tar names
application: Use apps/<cli>/VERSION plus <cli>-v<version> tag checks so releases are independently scriptable without cross-CLI coupling.

learning: When exposing custom Zig build steps to Homebrew formulas, make each step depend on install-artifact steps (not compile steps) so expected binaries land in zig-out/bin.
evidence: brew reinstall seq initially failed with ENOENT zig-out/bin/seq after zig build build-seq; fixed by wiring build-seq/build-lift/build-cas to addInstallArtifact steps in skills-zig/build.zig
application: For release and package automation, verify zig build <custom-step> produces install outputs before formula bin.install paths are finalized.

learning: For Homebrew proof of non-local sourcing, formulas must avoid file:// URLs and use remote git/tag URLs; verify via brew info urls.stable.url after reinstall.
evidence: brew info --json=v2 seq/lift/cas now reports url=https://github.com/tkersey/skills-zig.git and grep found no file:// path in active tap formulas
application: Use a post-install proof check that includes formula URL grep + brew info URL fields + Cellar symlink targets when users ask for Homebrew-only sourcing.

learning: For Zig CLI wrappers that delegate to scripts, centralize help-flag detection, script-path resolution, and command launching in libs/core to eliminate drift across apps.
evidence: Added libs/core/src/delegate_helpers.zig and removed duplicated helper blocks from cron/puff/learnings/append_learning wrappers.
zig test libs/core/src/delegate_helpers.zig passed with fuzz + allocation-failure signals; zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast passed.
application: Use core_delegate for future wrapper CLIs and keep wrapper files focused on usage text + error context.

learning: In the skills-zig monorepo, release only apps with actual code diffs, and require per-app build plus --help smoke before tagging and Homebrew tap updates.
evidence: Changed apps discovered by git status: cron, puff, learnings; build/test green via zig test delegate_helpers and zig build build-cron build-puff build-learnings.
application: Map changed apps to Formula/<app>.rb and publish matching tags/releases before brew upgrade/test.

learning: For Homebrew formulas that package multi-binary Zig tools, expose an explicit dispatcher binary (for example cas) when users expect subcommand UX (cas smoke_check), and test both direct and dispatched help paths.
evidence: cas formula installed only cas_instance_runner/cas_smoke_check, so command -v cas was empty despite package being installed; adding cas dispatcher and formula test resolved discoverability.
application: When adding subcommand UX, ship dispatcher in build-cas, include it in bin.install, and verify with brew test plus command -v checks.

learning: When replacing std.json hot-loop parsing in token_events, keep a std.json reference parser in tests and fuzz parity against it to preserve semantics while moving to a zero-allocation scanner.
evidence: apps/seq/src/datasets/token_events.zig now uses a structured scanner without per-line std.json allocations and includes parseTokenCountLineStdJson differential tests plus a std.testing.fuzz parity target.
application: For future parser hot-path rewrites, require differential corpus/fuzz parity and allocation-failure coverage in the same patch before cutover.

learning: When matching JSON object keys/selector strings in zero-allocation scanners, compare decoded JSON string content (including \u escapes and surrogate pairs), not raw bytes.
evidence: apps/seq/src/datasets/token_events.zig switched objectFieldValueSlice and fieldEqString to jsonStringContentEquals, and added parseTokenCountLine parity coverage with escaped keys/values.
cd apps/seq && zig build test passed after the change.
application: For future fast-path JSON scanners, require escape-aware key/value comparison helpers plus a differential test with escaped JSON forms before declaring parser parity.

learning: When extracting JSON string fields in zero-allocation scanners, decode escapes before deriving secondary fields (for example day/month from timestamp) to keep semantic parity with std.json.
evidence: apps/seq/src/datasets/token_events.zig now decodes timestamp through jsonDecodeStringInto before writing row.timestamp/day/month.
Added unicode/escape edge-case tests for jsonDecodeStringInto and parseTokenCountLine parity; cd apps/seq && zig build test passed.
application: For future fast-path parsers, pair escape-decoding helpers with direct edge-case tests (surrogates, malformed escapes, escaped non-required strings) whenever decoded text drives derived fields.

learning: For JSONL hot-path parser upgrades, pair structural parser changes (one-pass field indexing + fixed-key inner-object parsing) with a local benchmark binary and CI gate in the same patch to prevent silent perf regressions.
evidence: apps/seq/src/datasets/token_events.zig now indexes root/payload/info objects once per line and uses parseUsageObjectFixed for total/last usage objects.
Added apps/seq/src/perf_parser.zig + apps/seq/scripts/perf/parser_gate.sh + PR CI step; local run reported speedup_pct=89.06 and alloc_call_reduction_pct=99.97.
application: When touching parser internals in seq, require zig build test plus parser_gate output thresholds before merge.

learning: When adding zero-allocation JSONL prefilters, keep them monotonic with the std.json reference parser and avoid requiring optional keys in the fast reject path.
evidence: zig build test (apps/seq) passed after removing the total_token_usage hard prefilter and adding parity coverage for missing totals.
bash scripts/perf/parser_gate.sh passed synthetic trend gate and corpus report mode.
application: For token_events/perf parser updates, gate cheap substring filters to required structural keys only, then validate with parity + perf harness.

learning: For Zig fuzz CI on module-wired tests, use direct zig test with -ffuzz plus explicit -M/--dep wiring; runtime --fuzz args passed through zig build test run steps are rejected by the test runner.
evidence: zig build test-cas-budget-governor -- --fuzz --test-filter 'fuzz governor' failed with 'panic: unrecognized command line argument'.

zig test --dep core_json --dep core_io -Mroot=apps/cas/scripts/budget_governor.zig -Mcore_json=libs/core/src/json_helpers.zig -Mcore_io=libs/core/src/io_helpers.zig -ffuzz --test-filter 'fuzz governor' passed; same pattern passed for seq fuzz tests.
application: For seq/cas Linux fuzz jobs, invoke zig test directly with -ffuzz and module wiring instead of forwarding runtime flags through zig build test.

learning: When hardening Zig CLIs, pair an artifact-backed perf trend gate with a Linux-only bounded fuzz job; keep local macOS validation on deterministic tests/build/perf until Zig fuzz runtime support stabilizes.
evidence: lift: zig build test-lift -Doptimize=ReleaseFast passed
lift: bash apps/lift/scripts/perf/bench_stats_gate.sh passed (p95_ns_per_line=89, p50_alloc_calls_per_round=34)
application: Apply this template to each CLI: add bench-* perf harness + perf/* baseline artifact + CI fuzz job with timeout and exit-124 allowance.

learning: When validating performance-gated Zig CLIs, run perf gates serially; concurrent gate runs can trigger false PerfGateFailed due shared CPU contention.
evidence: Concurrent run of cas/lift/seq gates produced transient CAS PerfGateFailed (p95_ns_per_eval=21162 > 19000)
Isolated rerun of CAS gate immediately passed (p95_ns_per_eval=18547)
application: Keep CI per-job isolation and run local perf-gate validations one target at a time after refactors.

learning: For app-local Zig sources, inject VERSION via build options module (app_meta.version) instead of @embedFile('../VERSION') to avoid package-path embed errors.
evidence: zig build build-seq failed with: embed of file outside package path for @embedFile('../VERSION') in apps/seq/src/main.zig.
application: Use addVersionModule(...) in build.zig/app build.zig and import app_meta.version in CLI entrypoints.

learning: In seq query execution, using std.mem.sort for sortRows removes the O(n^2) insertion-sort path while preserving stable multi-key ordering semantics.
evidence: 2026-02-24: zig build test (apps/seq) passed after sortRows optimization.
2026-02-24: zig build bench -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -- --config perf/frozen/workload_config.json -> speedup_pct=22.52 status=PASS.
application: For sort-heavy query hotspots, prefer std.mem.sort/block with a comparator adapter and protect behavior with tie-order and null-order regression tests.

learning: Seq releases in skills-zig still require a separate homebrew-tap formula bump; release workflows do not auto-sync tap formulas.
evidence: 2026-02-24: docs/release/README.md Homebrew Tap Handoff states tap maintenance is separate.
2026-02-24: completed seq-v0.2.6 release and separate homebrew-tap commit 328e93e for Formula/seq.rb.
application: After seq tag publish succeeds, update homebrew-tap Formula/seq.rb version and both SHA256 values, then verify with brew update + brew upgrade --formula tkersey/tap/seq.

learning: When CAS approval surfaces expand, update both proxy policy flags and Zig pass-through flags in the same release to avoid runtime drift.
evidence: cas-v0.2.7 added --skill-approval plumbing in apps/cas/scripts/cas_proxy_client.zig and cas_instance_runner.zig with successful release workflow 22376832255.
application: For future app-server serverRequest additions, patch proxy handling + wrapper args + help/docs before tagging, then update homebrew formula checksums from release assets.

learning: When Lift Python wrappers gain compare/CI or report-template fields, mirror the same CLI surface in Zig before cutting tags so Homebrew binaries stay contract-parity.
evidence: lift-v0.2.6 adds --compare/--ci-samples/--ci-alpha/--seed to bench_stats.zig and adds Validation/Lift Compliance sections to perf_report.zig.
application: Before tagging lift-v*, run zig build test-lift + sample compare/json parity check against codex/skills/lift Python scripts.

learning: For CAS Zig tooling, remove Node dependency by speaking directly to codex app-server (initialize/initialized handshake + request/response loop) inside cas_proxy_client.zig.
evidence: zig build build-cas (exit 0)
zig build test-cas-budget-governor (exit 0)
zig build run-cas-smoke-check -- --cwd /Users/tk/workspace/tk/skills-zig --json (ok=true)
application: When CAS wrapper scripts shell to node, port handshake/request flow into Zig client first, then preserve approval auto-response semantics.

learning: For CAS releases in skills-zig, treat publish and tap propagation as separate gates: release tag/workflow success first, then homebrew-tap formula bump with both platform sha256 values and local brew upgrade/test proof.
evidence: skills-zig tag cas-v0.2.8 pushed; Release cas workflow run 22425147438 concluded success
GitHub release cas-v0.2.8 published with darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64 tarballs
homebrew-tap commit 52e0bd9 updates Formula/cas.rb to 0.2.8 and brew upgrade/test passed locally
application: In future CAS releases, do not assume release workflow updates the tap automatically; always push a distinct tap commit and verify brew upgrade + brew test.

learning: When app-server server-request surfaces change, update cas_proxy_client in the same patch by removing deprecated branches and selecting command auto-approvals from availableDecisions before fallback defaults.
evidence: zig build build-cas -Doptimize=ReleaseFast && zig build test-cas-budget-governor && zig build run-cas-smoke-check -- --cwd /Users/tk/workspace/tk/rs/codex --json all passed during cas 0.2.9 cut
release-cas workflow run 22445592756 completed success for tag cas-v0.2.9 before tap bump
application: At CAS release time, diff protocol/common.rs server requests first, then align cas_proxy_client + cas_instance_runner options before tagging and tap update.

learning: For seq query, keep op=regex as a documented regex-like subset with alternation support and fail-fast on unsupported metacharacters, and pair it with regex_any/contains_any for explicit OR semantics.
evidence: zig build test passed after adding regex alternation, regex_any/contains_any, and fail-fast tests in apps/seq/src/query/engine.zig
scripts/parity/run_diff.sh --root testdata/golden/sessions reported total=7 passed=7 failed=0 with new alternation/regex_any parity specs
application: When adding query operators in Zig, update Python oracle behavior and parity matrix in the same change to prevent silent cross-runtime drift.

learning: For tap updates done GitHub-only, run brew audit --strict after merge; if Formula uses on_macos/on_linux URL+sha blocks, switch to if OS.mac? / else layout to satisfy strict audit while keeping release checksums unchanged.
evidence: homebrew-tap PR #4 bumped seq to 0.2.7 and checksums, but brew audit --strict reported on_macos/on_linux URL+sha violations
homebrew-tap PR #5 changed Formula/seq.rb to if OS.mac? / else and brew audit --strict then passed
application: In future release handoffs, include an explicit strict-audit gate after tap merge and fix DSL shape via GitHub PR before declaring release complete.

learning: For lift parity checks, keep cross-runtime orchestration in run_diff.sh and expose explicit flags so harness config is reproducible without env-only tuning.
evidence: bash apps/lift/scripts/parity/run_diff.sh --help exposes --py-scripts-dir/--baseline/--variant/--build-mode.
bash apps/lift/scripts/parity/run_diff.sh --build-mode if-missing returned lift parity ok.
application: Use the shell harness for Zig-vs-Python parity orchestration and keep Zig binaries focused on production data-path behavior.

learning: When Python parity harnesses are intentionally retired, remove the harness files and docs in the same change because stale validation steps otherwise cause false migration expectations.
evidence: No remaining references: rg -n 'run_diff\.sh|LIFT_PARITY_' apps/lift README.md .github/workflows returned no matches.
Validation after removal: zig build build-lift -Doptimize=ReleaseFast and zig build test-lift both exited 0.
application: During runtime migrations, delete deprecated parity entrypoints and documentation together, then prove the Zig-native build/test path still passes.

learning: For lift releases, publish tag/workflow first and then bump tkersey/homebrew-tap in a second gate because Homebrew upgrade proof otherwise stays pinned to the prior formula revision.
evidence: skills-zig release run 22502337174 for lift-v0.2.7 completed success with darwin+linux assets and published release.
brew audit --strict tkersey/tap/lift initially failed on on_macos/on_linux url+sha, then passed after Formula/lift.rb switched to if OS.mac? / else at tap commit 1161060.
application: When cutting future lift versions, capture release asset digests, push tap checksum/layout update, run brew update + brew audit --strict + brew upgrade, and only then declare release complete.

learning: When expanding mesh lane fanout contracts, update budget/replay outputs and run_csv required headers in the same patch before tagging, so release assets and tap formula stay schema-consistent.
evidence: zig build test-mesh && zig build build-mesh && zig build run-mesh -- budget/wave/run_csv all passed locally for triplet fields.
Release run 22526121758 for mesh-v0.1.1 completed success on darwin-arm64 + linux-x86_64 and publish succeeded.
homebrew-tap Formula/mesh.rb bumped to 0.1.1 with release SHA256s and brew audit --strict tkersey/tap/mesh passed.
application: For future mesh releases, treat CLI schema, release tag, and tap checksum update as one gate and block release until all three checks are green.

learning: When upgrading mesh runtime contracts, update header requirements, the wave CSV emitter, and the run_csv parser in one patch to avoid schema drift.
evidence: zig build test-mesh passed after synchronized header plus emitter plus parser updates in apps/mesh/scripts/mesh.zig
zig build build-mesh passed with streaming lane expansion and new required CSV fields
application: For future mesh contract revisions, patch required headers, emission columns, and parsing defaults together, then run test-mesh and build-mesh before handoff.

learning: When a mesh release changes the runtime CSV schema, run four release checkpoints in order (Zig test/build, tagged GitHub release with asset SHAs, tap formula bump with strict audit, and local brew upgrade with version/help checks) because skipping a checkpoint can leave formula metadata and installed binaries out of sync.
evidence: mesh-v0.1.2 tag pushed and release-mesh workflow run 22534245161 succeeded with darwin/linux assets.
Formula/mesh.rb updated to 0.1.2 with new SHA256 values and brew audit --strict tkersey/tap/mesh passed.
brew upgrade tkersey/tap/mesh moved local install to 0.1.2; mesh --version and help marker both matched.
application: Apply this same ordered checklist to every future mesh release before marking propagation complete.

learning: When proving mesh orchestration runtime behavior, run spawn_agents_on_csv on mesh-generated batches and parse result_json for decision/proof fields because those fields are not flattened as top-level CSV columns.
evidence: spawn_agents_on_csv coder batch job fc96fd83-011a-4e3c-8d5c-7b8f98ac9bf2 completed 3/3 with v2 result_json payloads.
Fixer quorum proof yielded accepts=2, blockers=0 on 3 rows (quorum_pass=True), and prover retry flow moved from proof_failed to proof_complete on replacement.
CAS integration checks passed: cas smoke_check ok=true and cas instance_runner thread/list requests_ok=2 requests_failed=0.
application: Use this same proof sequence (coder batch, fixer quorum check, prover retry replacement, CAS smoke + instance runner) when validating future mesh orchestration releases.

learning: For CAS hardening in skills-zig, keep CI and local validation aligned on an aggregate 'zig build test-cas' step that includes budget_governor, cas_smoke_check, cas_instance_runner, and cas_proxy_client tests.
evidence: zig build test-cas
build.zig test-cas step now depends on test-cas-budget-governor,test-cas-smoke-check,test-cas-instance-runner,test-cas-proxy-client
.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml uses zig build test-cas
application: When CAS scripts change, wire each script root into build.zig test steps and have pr-ci run only the aggregate test-cas gate to avoid coverage drift.

learning: When writing seq opencode golden fixtures, set source=jsonl explicitly in command flags/spec params because source=auto will prefer a developer-local opencode.db and break deterministic assertions.
evidence: During zig build test, golden opencode-prompts read host DB rows instead of fixture rows until source=jsonl was set.
application: For fixture-based opencode tests, always pin source=jsonl plus opencode_path in both direct command tests and query-spec JSON files to prevent host-environment drift.

learning: When shipping seq releases, gate completion on three checkpoints in order: tag-triggered release workflow success, homebrew-tap formula bump with both platform SHA256s, and local brew upgrade/test/version proof to avoid claiming ship-complete too early.
evidence: seq-v0.2.13 completed on skills-zig run 22630943567; homebrew-tap commit 059450a updated Formula/seq.rb; brew upgrade installed seq 0.2.13 and brew test passed.
application: For future seq cuts, always capture run id + release URL + tap commit SHA + local brew proof in the same handoff.

learning: When adding zlinter to a multi-binary build.zig, gate lint graph construction behind an opt-in build option and invoke it only from the lint step, because unconditional lint dependency initialization can crash non-lint release builds.
evidence: Release mesh run 22688003159 failed in Build mesh binary due to zlinter->zls dependency initialization during non-lint build.
After switching lint to a proxy command with -Denable_zlinter=true, mesh release run 22688090063 completed successfully.
application: Use a default lint proxy step that re-invokes zig build lint with an internal enable flag so release/build steps remain free of lint-only dependency setup.

learning: When adding seq diagnostics for rollout JSONL, prefer parsing response_item function_call/function_call_output pairs by call_id and deriving running/exited/wall-time markers from output text, because this avoids brittle shell-only hang checks.
evidence: apps/seq/src/commands/mod.zig: collectInvocationRecordsFromSession + parseOutputMarkers + cmdQueryDiagnose
application: Reuse the shared invocation lifecycle parser when introducing new seq diagnostic commands so fail gates stay deterministic and parser logic is not duplicated.

learning: When learnings analytics need Codex session parsing, prefer exporting datasets through seq_bundle and importing from that bundle, because relative cross-module imports can fail Zig module-path constraints.
evidence: apps/seq/src/bundle.zig:4 exports messages_dataset.
zig build test-learnings passed on 2026-03-05.
./zig-out/bin/learnings quality-audit --path .learnings.jsonl --format json returned metrics.
application: For new learnings commands that inspect sessions, add the dataset export in apps/seq/src/bundle.zig, import it from learnings.zig, then validate with zig build test-learnings and command smoke checks.

learning: When querying high-volume opencode datasets, prefer collector-level pushdown of where/sort/limit before query.execute to avoid full-scan latency and apparent hangs.
evidence: Implemented collectDatasetRowsForSpec + applyOpencodePromptPushdown/applyOpencodeEventPushdown and collector-side filters/limits in apps/seq/src/commands/mod.zig and apps/seq/src/datasets/opencode_{prompts,events}.zig.
application: For future dataset additions, add collector pushdown hooks first, then run query-engine aggregation on the reduced row set.

learning: When optimizing session-root analytics, prefer path-day pushdown before file reads and verify the entry-path shape (including leading './'), because subtle path-shape mismatches can silently disable the intended speedup.
evidence: apps/learnings/scripts/learnings.zig:1709 applies sessionDayFromEntryPath pushdown before file reads.
apps/learnings/scripts/learnings.zig:1812 handles leading './' segments in sessionDayFromEntryPath.
After zig build build-learnings, value-report with full sessions root and since/until 2026-03-05 completed in real 0.51s.
application: For rollout JSONL walkers, parse and normalize entry.path segments first, filter by since/until before readFileAlloc, then rebuild binaries before timing to avoid stale performance conclusions.

learning: When tag-triggered release workflows fail to start, prefer a release fallback that still preserves tag-aligned artifacts and tap SHAs, because formula propagation must not block on workflow-trigger drift.
evidence: Tag pushes seq-v0.2.14 and learnings-v0.1.8 created refs but no new release workflow runs appeared in gh run list.
Created releases manually: https://github.com/tkersey/skills-zig/releases/tag/seq-v0.2.14 and .../learnings-v0.1.8 with both darwin/linux assets.
homebrew-tap commit 84bce3b updated Formula/seq.rb and Formula/learnings.rb; brew audit --strict, brew upgrade, and brew test passed.
application: For urgent seq/learnings cuts, publish releases directly with gh release create from verified darwin/linux tarballs, then update homebrew-tap formulas and prove with brew audit/upgrade/test.

learning: When validating tag-triggered releases, prefer checking queued runs and GitHub Status before assuming workflows did not trigger, because default run views can hide queued jobs during Actions outages.
evidence: Runs 22727600790 (seq-v0.2.14) and 22727603269 (learnings-v0.1.8) were queued with no steps while githubstatus reported Actions major_outage on 2026-03-05.
docs/release/README.md now includes queue triage and outage fallback commands.
application: For release triage, run gh run list --status queued for the specific workflow/tag, inspect gh run view job states, and use githubstatus API as a gate before falling back to manual release publishing.

learning: When adding a new Zig CLI under apps/ in skills-zig, add the app path trigger, paths-filter output, and dedicated build/test job to .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml because release/docs wiring alone otherwise leaves the CLI outside shared PR coverage.
evidence: Added apps/parse-arch path trigger, paths-filter output, and parse-arch build/test job in .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml; verified yaml-ok and zig build test-parse-arch.
application: For each new app, sync PR CI inventory at the same time as README and release workflow updates to prevent app-local changes from skipping monorepo PR validation.

learning: When promoting an app-local Zig test suite into a repo-root build step, set the run artifact cwd to the app directory because fixture-relative tests can fail under the monorepo root even when the app-local test step passes.
evidence: Root zig build test initially failed after adding test-seq because seq golden and fuzz fixtures resolved relative to apps/seq. Setting run_seq_tests.setCwd(b.path("apps/seq")) in build.zig fixed the root-owned test step, and both zig build test and cd apps/seq && zig build test then passed.
application: For future monorepo test fan-in work, treat cwd as part of the test contract and pin it explicitly for suites that read app-local testdata or fuzz corpora.

learning: When factoring monorepo Zig build helpers, keep top-level step registration single-owned because re-wrapping a helper that already creates a named step can panic with duplicate step names during zig build.
evidence: Extracting seq test wiring into addTestStepWithOptions initially left a second b.step("test-seq") wrapper in build.zig, and zig build test panicked with 'A top-level step with name "test-seq" already exists'. Removing the redundant wrapper restored zig build test and zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0.
application: When extracting build-step helpers in skills-zig, let the helper own named step creation and have aggregate steps depend on the returned run step unless a second public step name is intentionally required.

learning: When a Zig monorepo root build repeats app names across build, test, and lint wiring, prefer defining one app registry in build.zig because otherwise a new app addition can update one surface and silently miss the others.
evidence: build.zig now defines app_surfaces with path, build_deps, and test_deps, derives build-* grouped steps from that registry, derives the root test fan-in from the same registry, and feeds buildLintStep from the same app list; zig build test and zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0 both passed afterward.
application: For future CLI additions in skills-zig, update the single app_surfaces registry first and let grouped build, root test, and lint surfaces derive from it rather than editing each surface independently.

learning: When a Zig monorepo root build has two linked sqlite/libc test surfaces, prefer routing both through one helper because otherwise linked-test setup can drift between apps even when the public step names stay the same.
evidence: build.zig previously used addTestStepWithOptions for seq but manual b.addTest/linkLibC/linkSystemLibrary wiring for cron. Converting cron to addTestStepWithOptions preserved test-cron while zig build test and zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0 still passed.
application: For future linked test additions in skills-zig, use addTestStepWithOptions for sqlite/libc test setup so root-owned app tests share one implementation path.

learning: When cutting multiple CLI releases from one skills-zig commit, prefer proving the local monorepo gates first, then tagging only the materially changed CLIs because shared build.zig changes can affect several surfaces while release intent still stays CLI-specific.
evidence: For commit cedf981, local zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0, zig build test, zig build build-seq build-cron -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Dtarget=native, ./zig-out/bin/seq --version -> 0.2.15, and ./zig-out/bin/cron --version -> 0.2.3 all passed before tagging seq-v0.2.15 and cron-v0.2.3. GitHub Actions runs 22824546631 and 22824546659 then published both releases successfully.
application: For future multi-CLI release cuts in skills-zig, derive the target CLI set from the materially changed runtime/build surfaces, prove the shared local gates once, and then tag only those CLI VERSION bumps that match the intended release scope.

learning: When CAS app-server support expands with new server-initiated request types, add native default handlers plus explicit CLI overrides before tagging, because otherwise protocol coverage and skill docs drift apart.
evidence: skills-zig commit fca7c71 added item/permissions/requestApproval, item/tool/requestUserInput, mcpServer/elicitation/request, and item/tool/call handling plus turn/start and turn/interrupt smoke checks on 2026-03-10.
release-cas workflow run 22904115999 published cas-v0.2.12 successfully on 2026-03-10.
homebrew-tap commit 53a8329 plus HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 brew audit/upgrade/test and cas --version proved 0.2.12 locally on 2026-03-10.
application: On the next CAS protocol expansion, update cas_proxy_client defaults, instance_runner override flags, smoke_check coverage, and downstream skill docs in one release cycle.

learning: When a repository-architecture collector under-reads library-style Zig repos, prefer scoring the combination of one source root plus multiple contract/proof surfaces before broadening docs weighting because it improves signal on SDK-style layouts without regressing app-oriented fixtures.
evidence: zig build run-parse-arch -- collect /Users/tk/workspace/tk/shift changed the top signal from weak pipeline noise to modular-monolith with evidence 'library contract surfaces: src plus bench, docs, examples, test'.
zig build run-parse-arch -- eval --suite apps/parse-arch/references/eval/suite.yaml passed all 11 fixtures after adding library-contract-surfaces.
application: For future parse-arch heuristic work, add repo-shape signals first and only then revisit broader docs/test weighting if representative weak repos still under-read.

learning: When a session-mining CLI already has per-session command parsing, prefer promoting that parser into queryable datasets and bounded-window flags instead of falling back to raw JSONL shell probes.
evidence: seq now exposes tool_invocations and tool_call_args from the Zig binary, and live queries against ~/.codex/sessions returned learnings recall command_text and workdir rows without jq or rg fallback.
zig build test and bash scripts/release/command_surface_gate.sh both passed in apps/seq after adding the new datasets and since/until command support.
application: For future seq-style mining surfaces, ship the parsed runtime data as first-class datasets and pair it with coarse path pushdown plus exact row filtering so large roots stay usable.

learning: When adding local-only perf regression tracking to skills-zig, prefer one repo-root runner with machine-local baselines and keep legacy benchmark drivers in report-only mode so compare is judged by the local wrapper instead of inherited gate noise.
evidence: uv run python scripts/perf/local_perf.py capture && compare passed across 38 cases after driver wrappers were switched to --report-only and noisy cases got explicit tolerances.
application: Use .perf-local/<machine-id>/baselines plus the root perf-list/perf-doctor/perf-capture/perf-compare commands for future refactor judging; keep CI on build/test only.

learning: When cutting over a local Zig perf workflow toward a native control plane, prefer making manifest, audit, report, and accept native first, while temporarily delegating capture and compare through a compatibility runner to preserve existing baselines during the transition.
evidence: The new perf_hub now owns manifest/audit/report/accept and fronts capture/compare through the existing local runner while preserving current case IDs and local artifacts.
application: Use a native-first compatibility cutover for future perf or tooling rewrites: move ownership and evidence surfaces first, then replace measurement backends after parity proof.

learning: When cutting over a local perf workflow to a native Zig control plane, land manifest/audit/report/accept first and keep capture/compare delegated until the native hub can prove parity without breaking existing baseline IDs.
evidence: zig build perf-manifest-local, perf-audit-local, perf-report-local, perf-accept-local, and perf-compare-local -- --target puff all passed after the hub began reading native seq/cron/st command definitions.
application: Introduce native perf_hub commands and case manifests first, then replace delegated measurement only after parity proof and baseline compatibility are stable.

learning: When seq forensic work keeps reaching for raw query, add a dedicated command surface and searchable memory dataset before tuning performance because command-shape and visibility can dominate perceived cost.
evidence: zig build test passed in apps/seq after adding artifact-search and memory_blocks
bash apps/seq/scripts/release/command_surface_gate.sh passed after artifact-search was added to the binary help surface
application: For future seq UX improvements in skills-zig, prefer purpose-built forensic surfaces plus scan stats over expanding generic query examples.

learning: When a seq command truncates ArrayList(query.Row) output, prefer a helper that deinitializes dropped rows before reducing len because direct len shrink leaks owned row keys and strings and shows up as GPA leak output in live CLI runs.
evidence: /Users/tk/.local/bin/seq query-diagnose --path /Users/tk/.codex/sessions/2026/03/11/rollout-2026-03-11T07-12-17-019cdd3d-bfb2-7fe1-ba4a-7fcf50668490.jsonl --threshold-ms 3000 --next-actions --limit 2 --format table stopped printing GPA leak diagnostics after trimQueryRows was added
application: For future seq commands that cap ArrayList(query.Row) output, use a deiniting trim helper instead of assigning items.len directly.

learning: When closing a native perf control-plane cutover in skills-zig, preserve the old matrix shape but move the public root commands to native Zig first; then keep the former runner only as a private parity oracle until the preserved matrix is green end-to-end.
evidence: perf_hub now owns the public manifest/audit/doctor/capture/compare/report/accept workflow, preserved-matrix native capture/compare are green, and cutover-status.json is emitted from the native report path.
application: Use the same compatibility-first cutover pattern for the remaining Wave B deep-driver work: keep public ownership native, preserve baseline continuity, and demote old orchestration to proof-only status until parity is proven.

learning: When a Wave B native perf slice lands cheap deep-driver families, prefer regenerating the residual dossier immediately so the remaining work is the live post-slice truth rather than the prior plan.
evidence: Native deep cron/st cases and broader seq compat cases were added, and perf-report-local now recomputes cutover-status.json from the current native state.
application: Re-run perf-report-local after each Wave B slice because it prevents stale residual planning and makes the next stop condition explicit.

learning: When a Wave B native perf expansion adds noisy-but-legitimate deep and compat cases, prefer case-specific tolerance adjustments after same-machine recapture instead of broad global slack, because it keeps the residual dossier accurate without weakening the whole matrix.
evidence: After landing deep cron/st cases and broader seq compat cases, only a handful of same-machine noisy cases needed localized tolerance increases before the full native compare matrix went green again.
application: Tune tolerances at the case level after a native recapture/compare pass so Wave B closes on a stable matrix and a truthful residual list.

learning: When a native perf backlog still contains both real missing families and noisy new deep-driver cases, prefer calibrating only the noisy cases first so the residual list shrinks to true functional gaps instead of compare jitter.
evidence: Wave B reduced the cutover-status residuals to remaining seq families after cron and st deep-driver cases were stabilized under the native control plane.
application: Keep the native public compare/report path green by tuning only the currently failing deep cases before moving on to the next residual family, because that prevents noise from obscuring the real backlog.

learning: When expanding a native perf matrix, prefer landing the native command paths before recalibrating case budgets because that separates missing-surface failures from same-machine noise.
evidence: Wave B landed native seq shallow cases plus cron/st deep cases, and the remaining full-matrix failures are threshold overshoots rather than missing artifacts or missing command seams.
application: Use a follow-up calibration pass to retune bursty helper and deep-driver cases after the native matrix shape stabilizes, because otherwise compare red does not tell you whether structure or thresholds are wrong.

learning: When a native Wave B perf slice turns the compare matrix green, prefer regenerating the cutover dossier immediately because it prevents stale residual planning and makes the remaining families explicit.
evidence: Native cron/st deep cases and broader seq compat coverage reduced cutover-status.json to the true seq-only residual set.
application: Regenerate cutover-status.json after each Wave B slice so the next perf wave is driven by the live residual set instead of an older plan.

learning: When a native Wave B perf program exhausts its residual families, prefer proving the empty residual dossier with one final full-matrix recapture and compare because it turns local progress into a trustworthy closure signal.
evidence: After landing native cron/st deep cases and the remaining seq compat families, perf-report-local emitted cutover-status.json with an empty wave_b_residuals list.
application: Use the empty residual dossier as the exact stop condition for a local native perf wave and avoid carrying informal leftover lists past that point.

learning: When promoting seq perf cases from subprocess compat to true native deep measurement, prefer a dedicated apps/seq/src/perf_cli.zig seam that calls commands.run with fixture-backed absolute paths and output files, because this keeps perf_hub on real in-process latency-plus-allocation measurements and avoids duplicating seq command logic in the control plane.
evidence: apps/seq/src/perf_cli.zig added runPerfCase for query/session/artifact/token/routing families
zig build test-seq -> ok
zig build test-perf-hub -> ok
zig build perf-capture-local -- --target seq- >/dev/null && zig build perf-compare-local -- --target seq- -> ok
application: For future seq perf upgrades, add or extend the app-local perf seam first, then flip perf_hub case descriptors and coverage status from shallow compat to native deep before recapturing baselines.

learning: When a perf case is promoted from latency-only to latency-plus-allocation comparison, prefer failing compare closed if the saved baseline lacks alloc metrics, because otherwise the new allocation regression guard is silently skipped and legacy baselines can report a false green.
evidence: tools/perf_hub.zig compareLatencyMetrics now rejects latency_alloc baselines missing p50_alloc_calls
zig build test-perf-hub -> ok
zig build perf-compare-local -- --target seq- -> ok
application: For future perf promotions, add the legacy-baseline guard in compare first, then recapture baselines before relying on the stronger measurement mode.

learning: When a perf family finishes a native deep cutover, prefer removing any now-unreachable compat setup and render branches from the control plane, because otherwise dead duplicate execution paths linger and raise audit cost without adding fallback value.
evidence: tools/perf_hub.zig CompatCases now keeps only seq-help and seq-parser-driver for seq compat coverage
tools/perf_hub.zig renderCompatRun no longer carries dead seq native-family branches
zig build test-perf-hub -> ok
zig build perf-capture-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-compare-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-report-local >/dev/null -> ok
application: After future native perf promotions, prune unreachable compat enums and switch arms in the same cleanup slice once proof shows the deep path is the only live execution path.

learning: When a private compatibility oracle is kept alongside a native perf control plane, prefer keeping case ids and setup names byte-aligned with the native hub, because otherwise review and debugging split across two taxonomies for the same surface.
evidence: scripts/perf/local_perf.py renamed cas_budget_driver to cas_budget_governor_driver to match tools/perf_hub.zig
uv run python scripts/perf/local_perf.py compare --target cas-budget-governor-driver -> PASS
zig build perf-compare-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-report-local >/dev/null -> ok
application: For future oracle retention, normalize names at the first drift point instead of letting public and private perf surfaces diverge semantically.

learning: When the native perf control plane is already the only public path, prefer deleting the retained Python oracle outright instead of keeping a private compatibility copy, because stale duplicate infrastructure keeps accumulating taxonomy drift without strengthening the validated workflow.
evidence: scripts/perf/local_perf.py deleted
rg -n 'local_perf.py|scripts/perf/local_perf.py' . -> no matches
zig build perf-capture-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-compare-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-report-local >/dev/null && zig build perf-accept-local >/dev/null -> ok
application: After future native cutovers, remove the superseded runner and scrub fixture references in the same cleanup pass once the public bundle is green.

learning: When closing a Homebrew release proof, prefer checking the formula-installed binary path explicitly if PATH may be shadowed by ~/.local/bin, because otherwise a stale user-local binary can make version verification look wrong after a successful upgrade.
evidence: which st -> /Users/tk/.local/bin/st while /opt/homebrew/bin/st --version -> 0.1.4
brew info tkersey/tap/st showed 0.1.4 installed
brew test tkersey/tap/st -> ok
application: For future brew release proofs, record both brew-installed path and shell-resolved path before concluding version mismatch or release failure.

learning: When evaluating generalized effects for skills-zig, prefer piloting them at command-boundary orchestration seams like seq artifact-search and opencode source fallback instead of pure query/render kernels, because the payoff is in coordinating sources and interpreters rather than wrapping direct data transforms.
evidence: apps/seq/src/commands/mod.zig: cmdQuery/cmdArtifactSearch/collectDatasetRowsForSpec orchestrate dataset choice, collection, and emission
apps/seq/src/datasets/opencode_prompts.zig: collect() falls back from db to jsonl under .auto source
libs/core/src/delegate_helpers.zig already centralizes interpreter selection and subprocess execution as an effect-shaped seam
application: For future effect work in skills-zig, start with explicit ops plus handler builders around source selection, fallback, exec, or validation; leave query engines and formatters as plain functions.

learning: When a seq forensic need has a strict artifact boundary but does not justify a new public dataset, add a dedicated top-level command backed by a private extractor and reuse the existing session path/time narrowing helpers.
evidence: Implemented `apps/seq/src/plan_blocks.zig` plus `plan-search` in `apps/seq/src/commands/mod.zig` without exposing a public `plan_blocks` dataset.
`zig build test`, a live `plan-search --repo /Users/tk/workspace/tk/shift` corpus query, and the command-surface gate all passed after the command landed.
application: For future artifact-specific retrieval surfaces in seq, prefer a command-first public contract and a private extractor when the user wants focused UX without widening `seq query` or `dataset-schema`.

learning: When releasing a new seq command surface, require an installed-binary help check and one live installed-command smoke after the tap bump, because repo-local tests and GitHub release success alone do not prove the published Homebrew formula exposes the new command.
evidence: Published seq-v0.2.19 from commit 34199e5, bumped homebrew-tap to commit f5b934e, and verified `/opt/homebrew/bin/seq --help` included `plan-search` after upgrade.
Ran `/opt/homebrew/bin/seq plan-search --root ~/.codex/sessions --repo /Users/tk/workspace/tk/shift --limit 1 --format table` after the brew upgrade and got a real installed-binary result.
application: For future seq releases, keep the proof chain as: tag/workflow success -> tap formula update -> brew upgrade/test -> installed `--help` -> installed live command smoke.

learning: When a Zig CLI is a one-shot query tool with many short-lived allocations, prefer an arena allocator in main over GeneralPurposeAllocator because process-lifetime bulk teardown can materially reduce query latency without changing output.
evidence: In /Users/tk/workspace/tk/skills-zig, changing apps/learnings/scripts/learnings.zig main allocator to ArenaAllocator(page_allocator) kept recall output identical to the installed binary while reducing recall p95 from 19.78 ms to 12.37 ms over 40 samples on /Users/tk/.dotfiles/.learnings.jsonl
The same allocator change improved installed-binary parity workloads for recent and query: recent p95 11.63 ms to 9.91 ms and query p95 11.53 ms to 10.14 ms over 30 samples each
application: For CLI commands that parse files, build rows, and exit, benchmark an arena-backed main allocator before deeper loop refactors; keep the change only if exact output and test gates stay clean.

learning: When fresh-parent detached CAS review returns a thread whose preview equals the parent-materialization bootstrap prompt, classify the run as incompatible_codex_review_runtime and downgrade the persisted compatibility verdict, because otherwise CAS records a completed compatible review for a thread that never entered review mode.
evidence: Live repro with ./zig-out/bin/cas review_session start --wait --cwd /Users/tk/workspace/tk/shift --base main --timeout-ms 15000 --json returned failureCode=incompatible_codex_review_runtime and compatibilityVerdict=incompatible after the guard patch.

Recent persisted review-session artifacts under ~/.codex/cas/review_sessions showed completed compatible records whose event logs only read the bootstrap prompt thread: Internal bootstrap for detached review parent materialization. Reply with OK only.
application: In cas_review_session.zig, carry thread preview through ReviewStatus and fail closed on bootstrap-thread substitution before treating detached review as successful or merely missing output.

learning: When seq token-window questions depend on local calendar days, prefer instant-based ISO timestamp comparison plus token-usage --tz rebucketing because raw day prefixes and lexical timestamp ordering miscount mixed-offset windows.
evidence: zig build test-seq
zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0
./zig-out/bin/seq token-usage --help
application: Implement timezone-aware token summaries in seq and keep generic query for lower-level accounting checks only.

learning: When multiple installable Zig CLIs drift on help banners and usage exits, prefer a shared HelpSurface plus exitUsageFailure in libs/core/src/cli_helpers.zig, because that fixes stderr/exit-2 behavior and installed-name help with mostly mechanical top-level patches.
evidence: After the helper migration, seq unknown commands, cas_smoke_check invalid args, mesh unknown commands, st unknown commands, and bench_stats bad args all surfaced non-zero usage failures with installed-name help.
application: When another shipped CLI drifts, migrate its main help/version path and top-level parse failure path to the shared helper before rewriting deeper parser internals or docs.

learning: When optimizing a skills-zig CLI with existing perf_hub coverage, prefer covered latency_alloc lanes with a concrete isomorphic lever, because that yields measurable wins quickly and avoids wasting effort on unprofiled or compatibility-only surfaces.
evidence: This pass improved four covered lanes on April 2 2026: seq-query-tool-calls allocs 192->187 and p50_ns 270542->262125; cron-show-deep allocs 17->11 and p50_ns 1506458->1465625; cas-budget-governor-driver allocs 11->8 and p95_ns_per_eval 20207->18131; lift-bench-stats-driver allocs 34->1 and p95_ns_per_line 112->88.
application: When the next optimization request arrives, capture covered lanes with perf_hub first, rank them by measured latency and alloc pressure, and only implement the lanes where the code reveals one specific behavior-preserving lever.

learning: When a skills-zig CLI can be built from source, add a fail-closed install-prefix guard in every build.zig that rejects custom --prefix, --prefix-exe-dir, and DESTDIR, because otherwise binaries can be installed into ~/.local/bin instead of flowing through the Homebrew tap release path.
evidence: The root build.zig and apps/seq/build.zig now panic unless install_prefix/install_path/exe_dir match repo-local zig-out paths and dest_dir is null.
Proof: repo-local builds succeeded, and both root and standalone seq builds failed immediately when invoked with a temporary --prefix.
application: Use the guard together with CI that expects redirected-install builds to fail to prevent future local-install regressions.

learning: When a Homebrew formula install fails because a skills-zig release tarball omits a declared binary, prefer fixing the release workflow and shipping a new patch release before retargeting the tap formula, because replacing the published asset in place would hide the packaging defect and make release provenance unreliable.
evidence: brew upgrade failed for lift 0.2.9 with ENOENT on lift-perf-bench-stats; gh release download confirmed the tarball only contained lift-perf-report and lift-bench-stats.
Fix: update .github/workflows/release-lift.yml to package lift-perf-bench-stats, bump apps/lift/VERSION to 0.2.10, release lift-v0.2.10, then retarget Formula/lift.rb and rerun brew upgrade/test.
application: Use this when release-to-tap proof exposes a missing packaged binary: treat the workflow/package contract as the source of truth and recover with a fresh patch release.

learning: When a skills-zig repo must guarantee releases for changed CLIs, require VERSION bumps for every release-relevant CLI surface in PR CI and auto-dispatch the matching release workflow from main whenever those VERSION files change, because version bumps without automation still depend on human tag pushes and changed CLI code can otherwise land unreleased.
evidence: Added .github/scripts/release_apps.sh plus a new pr-ci release-contract job that fails when release-relevant CLI changes do not also modify apps/<cli>/VERSION.
Added .github/workflows/auto-release.yml and workflow_dispatch support across all release-*.yml files so pushes to main can create missing tags and dispatch the per-CLI release jobs automatically.
application: Use the shared detector for both PR and main-branch enforcement so the release policy is consistent and conservative across app-local, shared build/core, and per-cli release-workflow changes.

learning: When a seq archaeology surface accepts rollout-summary targeting, require a full relative or absolute path and fail closed on basename-only input, because multiple memory-block headings from one summary file or reused basenames can otherwise make provenance look authoritative when the selector is under-specified.
evidence: The memory-provenance implementation initially accepted basename-only rollout-summary input and a fixed-point review surfaced this as a material misuse path.
The final seq behavior now requires full relative/absolute rollout-summary paths and returns a non-zero error for basename-only input while preserving the happy path for full paths.
application: Use this guard for future archaeology/provenance CLI surfaces that bind high-confidence output to file selectors.

learning: When migrating CAS transport code to Zig 0.16, move stdio/websocket/process handling onto the explicit Io surface (Io.net streams, file.reader/file.writeStreamingAll, Child.kill(io), io.random, monotonic clock helpers) and stop the fix wave once build failures move into adjacent binaries outside the owned transport files.
evidence: Owned files apps/cas/scripts/cas_proxy_client.zig, cas_websocket_transport.zig, and cas_instance_runner.zig now pass focused validation via zig build test-cas-proxy-client and zig build test-cas-instance-runner.

After the transport migration, zig build build-cas fails only in non-owned files: cas_smoke_check.zig (std.time.timestamp), cas_review_session.zig (std.fs.openDirAbsolute), and cas_conformance_suite.zig (std.fs.makeDirAbsolute).
application: For future CAS Zig 0.16 migrations, patch the transport surface first, validate it with focused test-cas-* lanes, then hand off any remaining build failures once the error frontier moves into neighboring binaries.

learning: When upgrading st Zig tests to 0.16, keep ObjectMap-based test fixtures on the allocator-threaded API (, , ) and replace tmpDir calls with to keep the suite compiling.
evidence: zig build test-st passed after updating apps/st/scripts/st.zig fixture helpers for ObjectMap and tmpDir realpath APIs.
application: For future 0.16 migrations in skills-zig CLIs, patch test helpers and teardown sites first before chasing higher-level runtime changes.

learning: When a skills-zig Zig 0.16 migration reaches a green root build, report fmt, lint, and test as separate closure gates and keep fixing them independently instead of treating compile success as full closure.
evidence: zig build now passes on the repo with Zig 0.16.0 after repeated std.Io/std.process/time API replacements across the root build path.

After build closure, zig fmt --check still fails on tracked files, zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0 remains fail-closed because zlinter is not upgraded, and zig build test still fails on test-only migration surfaces.
application: When closing future Zig upgrades in this repo, use build -> fmt -> lint -> test as distinct proof lanes and state which lanes are still open.

learning: When skills-zig Zig 0.16 lint closure is blocked by zlinter stderr from zls translate-c, first isolate the remaining @cImport users and prefer excluding the single file from lint over a wider rewrite if std lacks the needed API.
evidence: zig build lint -- --fix -> clean exit but emitted translate-c OutOfMemory until time_utils.zig was excluded
rg -n '@cImport|@cInclude|@cDefine|@cUndef' apps libs tools build.zig -g'*.zig' -> only apps/seq/src/time_utils.zig remained
zig build lint -- --max-warnings 0 -> No issues after excluding apps/seq/src/time_utils.zig
application: For minimal 0.16 migrations, keep the lint surface path-based and carve out the one @cImport file when translate-c noise is toolchain-driven rather than a repo lint violation.

learning: When testing memory digest append integration, prefer temp HOME isolation because auto-refresh should not touch live memory resources.
evidence: zig-out/bin/learnings append temp integration passed
application: Use temp HOME for append auto-refresh regression checks.

learning: When a CLI writes generated memory-extension resources, prefer resolving CODEX_HOME explicitly and testing with a temp CODEX_HOME because HOME fallbacks can silently target the wrong resource path.
evidence: CODEX_HOME=temp learnings memory-digest wrote memories_extensions/learnings/resources/latest_learnings_digest.md and old learnings_digest.md was absent.
CODEX_HOME=temp learnings append wrote latest_learnings_digest.md during auto-refresh with rc=0.
application: For future learnings digest changes, verify both direct digest and append auto-refresh against a temp CODEX_HOME before shipping.

learning: When a release tag triggers both push and workflow-dispatch publish runs, prefer waiting for all release runs on the commit to finish before updating Homebrew SHA256 values because the later publish can replace same-version assets.
evidence: learnings-v0.1.16 push release first published darwin sha256 66db20... and linux sha256 63915..., then workflow_dispatch republished final darwin sha256 08c58... and linux sha256 5fe9...
Homebrew tap Formula/learnings.rb was updated only after gh run watch succeeded for both release runs and gh release view returned final asset digests.
application: For future skills-zig CLI releases, inspect gh run list for duplicate release workflows and recompute release asset digests after the last successful publish before committing Homebrew formula checksums.

learning: When changing st projection command surfaces, prefer one shared projection helper plus command-table removal of superseded aliases because hook, reverse-sync, and mutation payload paths otherwise drift.
evidence: apps/st/scripts/st.zig: PlanSyncVersion v3, prime/assert-projection/reconcile-codex/import-proposed-plan command table, removed emit-plan-sync/emit-update-plan/import-update-plan command names; zig build test-st and build-st pass.
application: For future st CLI projection changes, wire new commands through computeProjectionResult first, then verify old command names fail and mutation plan_sync rows remain Codex-safe.

learning: When adding new CLI command surfaces with advertised flags, run a read-only CLI audit before closure because compile/smoke tests can miss scriptability contract drift such as accepted-but-ignored options or wrong output formats.
evidence: seq trace fixed-point audit found tail --events ignored, session-detail accepted jsonl but emitted JSON object, invalid finite filters returned empty success, and --include-tools had no observable output delta; repaired before final ReleaseFast proof.
application: For future seq or Zig CLI additions, include an audit pass plus focused checks for format matrices, finite enum validation, and each advertised flag's observable output change.

learning: When a Zig 0.16 CLI launches child processes, thread std.process.Init.io through spawn/run paths instead of std.Io.Threaded.global_single_threaded.io because the global single-threaded allocator is .failing and child spawn can fail with OutOfMemory.
evidence: apps/cas/scripts/cas_proxy_client.zig spawned codex app-server through global_single_threaded and live cas_smoke_check failed at std/Io/Threaded.zig spawnPosix with error.OutOfMemory.
After passing init.io into CAS ClientOptions and managed websocket startup, zig build test-cas and zig build build-cas -Doptimize=ReleaseFast passed.
application: For Zig 0.16 app CLIs, pass init.io from main into modules that spawn subprocesses or use std.process.run; reserve global_single_threaded for simple file/stdout operations that do not allocate inside Io.

learning: When a Zig 0.16 CLI spawns child processes, thread the process Init io into std.process.run paths because global_single_threaded uses a failing allocator for process spawn internals.
evidence: cron run-due and scheduler status returned OutOfMemory until apps/cron/scripts/cron.zig passed init.io into runCodexExec/runCommandCapture.
zig build test-cron hung under --listen until the new cmdUpdate regression test silenced command stdout with silenceStdout.
application: For future Zig CLI fixes, make IO capability propagation and test-runner stdout hygiene explicit proof points before declaring closure.

learning: When adding seq goal-run analytics, classify Codex-review goal objectives by explicit Codex/native review-loop terms rather than generic review wording, and do not treat review invocations inside goals as contamination.
evidence: goal-audit classifier fixed after root-owned review found generic review false positives and resolve review-invocation contamination.
application: For future seq goal/session forensics surfaces, keep objective classifiers narrow and keep contamination checks scoped to the objective kind being audited.

learning: When adding new values to seq command enums, prefer appending them before the terminal unknown value instead of inserting in the middle because CI Zig cache reuse can expose stale enum-ordinal mismatches across independently cached test objects.
evidence: GitHub PR CI seq job failed on Linux with --summary unsupported for existing commands after inserting goal_audit mid-enum; moving goal_audit to an append-only enum position preserved existing ordinals and kept local tests green.
application: For future Zig CLI command additions, treat public command enums as cache/ABI-sensitive within the build graph and make additive enum changes append-only unless a clean-cache migration is part of the proof.

learning: When a Linux seq CI failure appears cache-shaped after a command enum change, prefer changing the dependent command validator source or clearing the CI Zig cache because lib-only enum movement may not invalidate restored test objects.
evidence: After moving goal_audit to an append-only enum position, GitHub seq CI still restored the prior failing commands.mod object; adding commandSupportsSummary inside commands/mod.zig forced the relevant validator object to rebuild while local app/root tests stayed green.
application: For future cached Zig CI failures, make the smallest source-level invalidation in the module named by the failing stack trace, then rerun local proof and remote checks.

learning: When Linux seq CI shows enum-switch option support disagreeing with @tagName(cmd), prefer a tag-name based capability check for that narrow validation path because restored Zig test objects can preserve a stale enum-switch decision while tag names still report the correct command.
evidence: PR #2 Linux seq test repeatedly reported --summary unsupported for token_usage/session_tooling/goal_audit even though unsupportedOption printed the correct @tagName(cmd); replacing the summary switch with tag-name comparisons passed local app/root tests and the failing seed.
application: Use this only for narrow CLI option capability gates with CI evidence; keep ordinary command dispatch on typed enums unless the failure log proves tag-name/equality drift.

learning: When optimizing Zig CLI session-inventory paths, profile the parser replacement before release and prefer prefix-based event classification over repeated full-line substring scans because large JSONL message bodies can make a summary parser slower than full std.json parsing.
evidence: sample(1) showed parseSessionTrace/std.json.Scanner dominated seq sessions --limit 500 before the parser change; the first summary parser regressed 7.66s to 9.54s; prefix classification then improved the same workload to 1.80s and --limit 5 to 0.06-0.09s.
application: For future seq trace optimizations, gate fast paths by exact CLI/query shape, profile a larger representative window, and verify the classifier skips response_item bodies before tagging.

learning: When a Zig 0.16 perf harness on macOS repeatedly runs child CLIs and only needs exit status, use a small posix_spawnp runner with redirected stdout/stderr instead of std.process.run; it can avoid spawn-time OutOfMemory while keeping capture stable.
evidence: perf-capture-local initially failed in tools/perf_hub.zig child capture with OutOfMemory; posix_spawnp runner made seq/cas compare and capture pass.
application: Apply this before widening perf coverage for CLI matrices, then profile to confirm the harness is waiting on child workloads rather than consuming CPU itself.
